meta.title: Every Season — Set 5
meta.subject: English Reading
meta.description: Challenge quiz for 'Every Season' — inference, theme, and comparisons.

questions.question: Why do geese fly south in autumn?
options: Because they like the color yellow of the ash trees.
To escape the cold winter and find food in warmer places.
To help chipmunks carry acorns to secret spots.
Because they want to wear jackets and hoods.
questions.explanation: Geese fly south in autumn because winter is coming. Warmer places in the south have more food and less freezing weather.

questions.question: Animals leave tracks in winter because the snow is soft and covers the ground.
questions.explanation: True! The soft snow acts like a blanket, capturing the footprints of animals as they walk across it.

questions.question: Why do chipmunks store acorns in a 'secret' spot?
options: So other animals cannot find and eat their winter food.
Because acorns are too heavy to carry to their homes.
Because they forget where they put their food.
To play a game with the geese.
questions.explanation: Storing food in a secret, hidden spot ensures that other hungry animals won't steal their acorns before winter.

questions.question: The author dislikes winter because it brings cold temperatures and icicles.
questions.explanation: False. The author says 'I Love Winter Too,' showing they enjoy the snow, ice, and winter activities.

questions.question: What does 'seeds scatter' in autumn help plants do?
options: It helps plants grow in new places when spring returns.
It feeds the shorebirds in the hot summer.
It keeps the trees warm under red oak jackets.
It makes the wind whip harder.
questions.explanation: When seeds scatter (spread out) in autumn, they can rest in the soil and grow into new plants in spring.

questions.question: In winter, snow _______ branches and buds. This keeps them covered.
questions.explanation: The snow covers the branches like a blanket, which is why the author uses the verb 'blankets.'

questions.question: Which season is described as the time to 'dig and plant'?
options: spring
summer
autumn
winter
questions.explanation: Spring is the season when the weather gets warmer and the soil softens, making it the perfect time to dig and plant seeds.

questions.question: Sort these things from the story into their main seasonal colors:
questions.explanation: Grass is green and icicles are clear/white. Pumpkins, maples (orange), ash (yellow), and oaks (red) represent warm autumn colors.

questions.question: 'Showers soak' in spring means that it rains a lot and makes the ground very wet.
questions.explanation: True. 'Showers' are rainfalls, and 'soak' means to make extremely wet. This rain helps seeds sprout.

questions.question: Arrange the words to show what chipmunks do:
questions.explanation: Correct sentence: 'Chipmunks store acorns in a secret spot.' This shows how they prepare for winter.

questions.question: Why do horses grow 'thick coats' only in winter?
options: Because they change their clothes every month.
Because the cold winter weather requires extra warmth.
Because they want to look pretty for spring.
Because they run faster in heavy coats.
questions.explanation: Horses grow thick coats of fur in winter to protect themselves from the freezing cold temperatures.

questions.question: Daffodils and crocuses open early, but lilacs open later and spread their _______ smell.
questions.explanation: The text states: 'lilacs spread their sweet smell' in the spring.

questions.question: Arrange the words to describe what winter cold brings:
questions.explanation: Correct sentence: 'The cold brings icicles and snowflakes that swirl.' This describes the cold winter scene.

questions.question: The story shows that nature goes through a continuous circle of seasons that returns to spring at the end.
questions.explanation: True. The story goes from spring, to summer, to autumn, to winter, and ends with 'But then spring comes... I Love Spring,' showing the circle of seasons starts again.

questions.question: How does the author show that summer is a hot season?
options: By mentioning hot chocolate and thick horse coats.
By mentioning wearing a straw hat, going barefoot, and eating ice cream.
By mentioning pulling up hoods and zipping up jackets.
By mentioning geese flying away to the south.
questions.explanation: Wearing a straw hat blocks the hot sun, going barefoot is only done when the ground is warm, and ice cream and lemonade keep us cool, showing summer is hot.
